questions.question: Which street artist's 'Girl with Balloon' partly shredded itself right after selling at auction in 2018?
questions.fun_fact: The half-shredded work was renamed 'Love is in the Bin' and later resold for far more than its original price.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Winnie-the-Pooh'?
questions.fun_fact: Pooh was inspired partly by a real bear called Winnipeg at London Zoo, after which he was named.

questions.question: Which famous Paris cathedral was badly damaged by a fire in April 2019?
questions.fun_fact: Its spire collapsed in the blaze, and the cathedral reopened in December 2024 after extensive restoration.

questions.question: Caravaggio is famous for dramatic contrasts of light and dark. What is this technique called?
questions.fun_fact: His violent personality matched his paintings, and he fled Rome in 1606 after killing a man.

questions.question: What was the name of Shakespeare's wife?
questions.fun_fact: In his will he left her only his 'second-best bed'.

questions.question: Picasso's 'Guernica' responds to the bombing of a Basque town during which conflict?
questions.fun_fact: The huge black-and-white canvas debuted at the 1937 World's Fair in Paris and is now in the Reina Sofía museum in Madrid.

questions.question: Who wrote the tragedy 'Romeo and Juliet'?
questions.fun_fact: The play is set in Verona, and Shakespeare probably wrote it in the mid-1590s.

questions.question: Monet painted his famous water lilies in his garden in which French village?
questions.fun_fact: He designed the pond himself, with a Japanese-style bridge, and painted it for roughly the last 30 years of his life.

questions.question: The Terracotta Army in China was buried to guard the tomb of which person?

answers.text: Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor

questions.fun_fact: Farmers digging a well found it in 1974, and the figures all have different faces.

questions.question: Which Dutch painter created 'The Starry Night' in 1889?
questions.fun_fact: He painted it from memory during the day, based on the view from his room at the asylum in Saint-Rémy, adding an imagined village.

questions.question: In 'Don Quixote', what does the hero famously charge at, believing them to be giants?
questions.fun_fact: Miguel de Cervantes published it in two parts, in 1605 and 1615, and it is often called the first modern novel.

questions.question: Which playwright wrote 'Waiting for Godot', in which two men wait for someone who never arrives?
questions.fun_fact: Beckett wrote it in French first, and it won him the Nobel Prize in 1969.

questions.question: In which Shakespeare play does the famous stage direction 'Exit, pursued by a bear' appear?
questions.fun_fact: Scholars debate whether a real bear or an actor in a costume played the part.

questions.question: Hokusai's 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa' is what kind of artwork?
questions.fun_fact: Mount Fuji is the small peak in the background, and the print belongs to a series of 36 views of the mountain.

questions.question: In Hemingway's 'The Old Man and the Sea', what giant fish does the old fisherman hook?
questions.fun_fact: The short novel won the 1953 Pulitzer Prize and helped Hemingway win the Nobel the following year.

questions.question: Which Flemish painter created the 'Arnolfini Portrait' in 1434, with a tiny mirror reflecting the room?
questions.fun_fact: Above the mirror he wrote 'Jan van Eyck was here', as if signing a witness statement.

questions.question: Artemisia Gentileschi, known for her dramatic 'Judith' paintings, worked in which art period?
questions.fun_fact: She was one of the first women admitted to the art academy in Florence.

questions.question: Which play contains the line 'All the world's a stage'?
questions.fun_fact: The speech is given by the melancholy Jaques and describes the seven ages of man.

questions.question: The Uffizi Gallery, home to Botticelli's 'Birth of Venus', is in which Italian city?
questions.fun_fact: 'Uffizi' means 'offices': the building was originally constructed to house the administration of the Medici family.

questions.question: El Greco, the Spanish Renaissance painter, was born on which island?
questions.fun_fact: His nickname simply means 'The Greek', and he spent most of his working life in Toledo.

questions.question: What is the name of Harry Potter's pet owl?
questions.fun_fact: Rowling reportedly found the name Hedwig in a book about medieval saints.

questions.question: Marcel Duchamp's notorious 1917 artwork 'Fountain' was a signed what?
questions.fun_fact: He signed it 'R. Mutt'; the original was lost, so the versions seen today are later replicas.

questions.question: Which Nigerian writer became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1986?
questions.fun_fact: He was jailed for almost two years during the Nigerian civil war after speaking out against the conflict.

questions.question: Leonardo's 'Vitruvian Man' drawing shows what?

answers.text: The ideal proportions of the human body

questions.fun_fact: The drawing appears on the Italian one-euro coin.

questions.question: Mary Shelley began 'Frankenstein' during a ghost-story challenge near which lake?
questions.fun_fact: The group, which included Lord Byron, was stuck indoors in 1816, the so-called 'Year Without a Summer'.

questions.question: Which French Impressionist is famous for his paintings of ballet dancers?
questions.fun_fact: He also made a wax sculpture of a young dancer that was dressed in a real cloth tutu.

questions.question: George Eliot, author of 'Middlemarch', was the pen name of a woman with which real name?
questions.fun_fact: She chose a male name so that her work would be taken seriously.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek playwright wrote 'Oedipus Rex'?
questions.fun_fact: Freud later used the title for his 'Oedipus complex'.

questions.question: Which Swedish author created Pippi Longstocking?
questions.fun_fact: She first invented the character as a story to cheer up her sick daughter.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Jane Eyre'?
questions.fun_fact: She published it in 1847 under the male pen name Currer Bell.

questions.question: In which Paris museum does the Mona Lisa hang?
questions.fun_fact: The painting was stolen in 1911 by a museum worker and only recovered two years later, which made it world famous.

questions.question: Which hero spends ten years trying to get home in Homer's 'Odyssey'?
questions.fun_fact: The poem includes the Cyclops and the Sirens, and the Romans called its hero Ulysses.

questions.question: René Magritte's painting of a pipe carries the caption 'This is not a...' what?
questions.fun_fact: The Belgian surrealist's point was that a painting of a pipe is an image, not a real pipe you can smoke.

questions.question: For which pharaoh was the Great Pyramid of Giza built?
questions.fun_fact: It was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for around 3,800 years.

questions.question: Which Irish writer wrote 'The Picture of Dorian Gray'?
questions.fun_fact: It was Wilde's only novel, and he wrote most of his famous plays afterwards.

questions.question: Which Dickens character famously asks, 'Please, sir, I want some more'?
questions.fun_fact: The scene takes place in a workhouse, and the book first appeared in monthly instalments in a magazine.

questions.question: Georges Seurat's 'A Sunday on La Grande Jatte' is made of thousands of tiny dots. What is the technique called?
questions.fun_fact: He worked on it for about two years, and viewers' eyes blend the dots into colours from a distance.

questions.question: Which famous musician won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016?
questions.fun_fact: He did not attend the ceremony but sent a speech to be read out, and gave his lecture later.

questions.question: What do the 'flying buttresses' on Gothic cathedrals do?

answers.text: Support the walls from the outside

questions.fun_fact: They let builders make walls taller and fill them with large stained-glass windows.

questions.question: In 'The Lord of the Rings', in which fiery mountain must the One Ring be destroyed?
questions.fun_fact: Tolkien was a close friend of C. S. Lewis, and the two met regularly in a writers' group called the Inklings.

questions.question: In which Shakespeare play does a man get turned into a donkey with fairy help?
questions.fun_fact: The man is Nick Bottom the weaver, and the fairy mischief-maker responsible is Puck.

questions.question: What does Jean Valjean steal at the start of 'Les Misérables'?
questions.fun_fact: He is sentenced to five years for the theft and ends up serving 19 after trying to escape.

questions.question: Which of King Lear's daughters is the youngest and the only one who is truly loyal?
questions.fun_fact: Her honest answer, that she loves him as a daughter should, is what angers Lear at the start.

questions.question: In 1993 Toni Morrison, author of 'Beloved', became the first African American woman to win which prize?
questions.fun_fact: The Nobel committee praised her novels for their visionary force and poetic import.

questions.question: The Metropolitan Museum of Art stands on the edge of which New York park?
questions.fun_fact: The museum opened in 1872 in a different building and moved to its current home in the 1880s.

questions.question: Which artist turned Campbell's soup cans into pop art in 1962?
questions.fun_fact: The original work consists of 32 canvases, one for each flavour the company sold at the time.

questions.question: Which famous Paris bookshop first published James Joyce's 'Ulysses' in 1922?
questions.fun_fact: The shop's American owner, Sylvia Beach, took on the book when other publishers refused it.

questions.question: Norman Rockwell was famous for painting covers for which American magazine?
questions.fun_fact: He painted over 300 covers for the magazine across a span of 47 years.

questions.question: What is the name of the failing salesman in Arthur Miller's 'Death of a Salesman'?
questions.fun_fact: The play premiered in 1949 and won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama.

questions.question: Which Japanese artist is famous for her polka dots and 'Infinity Mirror Rooms'?
questions.fun_fact: She has lived by choice in a psychiatric hospital in Tokyo since the 1970s and still works daily.

questions.question: How old was Pablo Picasso when he died?
questions.fun_fact: Picasso worked almost until the end: tens of thousands of his paintings, ceramics and prints survive from a career of more than 75 years.

questions.question: Velázquez's 'Las Meninas' hangs in which Madrid museum?
questions.fun_fact: Velázquez painted himself into the scene, standing at a large canvas on the left.

questions.question: In his old age, Henri Matisse created large artworks mainly by doing what?

answers.text: Cutting shapes out of painted paper

questions.fun_fact: Ill health kept him in a chair, so he called it 'painting with scissors'.

questions.question: What is the name of the protagonist of Orwell's 'Nineteen Eighty-Four'?
questions.fun_fact: Orwell finished the book in 1948 on a remote Scottish island called Jura, and flipped the year digits for the title.

questions.question: Which English painter created 'The Hay Wain', showing a cart crossing a river in Suffolk?
questions.fun_fact: The painting won a gold medal at the Paris Salon of 1824 and strongly influenced French landscape painters.

questions.question: Which Romanian-born sculptor made the polished bronze 'Bird in Space'?
questions.fun_fact: US customs once treated a Brâncuși sculpture as a metal object and charged duty, and he took the case to court in 1928.

questions.question: In 'Sense and Sensibility', Elinor Dashwood's younger sister is called what?
questions.fun_fact: It was Jane Austen's first published novel, in 1811.

questions.question: On which London street is Sherlock Holmes's fictional address at number 221B?
questions.fun_fact: When the stories appeared, no 221B existed; today a museum there claims the address.

questions.question: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel between 1508 and 1512?
questions.fun_fact: Michelangelo saw himself as a sculptor and reportedly complained about the job, yet it became his most famous painted work.

questions.question: Which art movement got its name from a Monet painting called 'Impression, Sunrise'?
questions.fun_fact: The critic Louis Leroy used the word mockingly in 1874, but the painters liked it and adopted it themselves.

questions.question: Which sculptor made the giant spider sculptures called 'Maman'?
questions.fun_fact: The spiders are about nine metres tall, and she meant them as a tribute to her mother, a tapestry restorer.

questions.question: In Kafka's 'The Metamorphosis', Gregor Samsa wakes up transformed into what?
questions.fun_fact: Kafka insisted that the insect never be shown on the book's cover.

questions.question: Where does the hero of Saint-Exupéry's 'The Little Prince' live?
questions.fun_fact: The prince's asteroid is called B-612, and the book is among the most translated ever written.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Charlie and the Chocolate Factory'?
questions.fun_fact: Dahl was a fighter pilot in the RAF during World War II before he became a writer.

questions.question: Which Dr. Seuss book was written using only 50 different words, after a bet?
questions.fun_fact: His publisher Bennett Cerf bet him that he could not write a book with so few words.

questions.question: In 'Oliver Twist', what is the nickname of the pickpocket Jack Dawkins?
questions.fun_fact: He is one of Fagin's gang, and the book's depiction of London's poor shocked Victorian readers.

questions.question: Which Belgian detective created by Agatha Christie relies on his 'little grey cells'?
questions.fun_fact: When Poirot was killed off in 1975, the New York Times printed an obituary, a rare honour for a fictional character.

questions.question: Who wrote the poem 'The Raven', with its refrain 'Nevermore'?
questions.fun_fact: Poe published it in 1845, and it made him famous almost overnight.

questions.question: Which British artist put a shark in a tank of formaldehyde and called it a work of art?
questions.fun_fact: The piece, made in 1991, was commissioned by the collector Charles Saatchi.

questions.question: What kind of animal is Napoleon in George Orwell's 'Animal Farm'?
questions.fun_fact: Napoleon is modelled on Stalin, while his rival Snowball stands for Trotsky.

questions.question: Who is the heroine of Suzanne Collins's 'The Hunger Games'?
questions.fun_fact: The first novel was published in 2008 and was inspired by Greek myth and reality TV.

questions.question: Which Victor Hugo novel features the bell-ringer Quasimodo?
questions.fun_fact: The book helped inspire a campaign to restore the neglected cathedral.

questions.question: How many sonnets are in Shakespeare's 1609 collection?
questions.fun_fact: Most of the sonnets address a young man and the later ones a mysterious 'Dark Lady'. Who either of them was is still unknown.

questions.question: Which Spanish surrealist painted melting clocks in 'The Persistence of Memory'?
questions.fun_fact: The painting is tiny, only about 24 by 33 centimetres, and hangs in the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

questions.question: In 'Lord of the Flies', what object do the stranded boys use to call meetings?
questions.fun_fact: William Golding won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1983.

questions.question: Which New York museum has a famous spiral ramp inside, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
questions.fun_fact: It opened in 1959, only six months after Wright's death.

questions.question: Pablo Picasso co-founded Cubism with which French painter?
questions.fun_fact: The two worked so closely around 1910 that Braque compared their partnership to mountaineers roped together.

questions.question: Which lawyer defends Tom Robinson in 'To Kill a Mockingbird'?
questions.fun_fact: Harper Lee's follow-up 'Go Set a Watchman' appeared only in 2015, decades after the original.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal was built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a tomb for whom?
questions.fun_fact: Construction took around 20 years and used white marble that was reportedly hauled in by elephants.

questions.question: The Sydney Opera House was designed by an architect from which country?
questions.fun_fact: Jørn Utzon resigned in 1966 amid disputes before it was finished and never saw the completed building.

questions.question: Which Dutch artist is famous for his impossible staircases and endlessly repeating patterns?
questions.fun_fact: His works such as 'Ascending and Descending' are popular with mathematicians as well as art fans.

questions.question: A traditional Japanese haiku follows which syllable pattern?
questions.fun_fact: Strictly speaking, Japanese haiku count sound units rather than syllables.

questions.question: James Joyce's 'Ulysses' takes place over a single day in which city?
questions.fun_fact: The day is 16 June 1904, which fans celebrate each year as Bloomsday.

questions.question: Which Scottish architect and designer created the Glasgow School of Art building?
questions.fun_fact: The building was damaged by serious fires in 2014 and 2018.

questions.question: Which French writer wrote 'The Stranger', which opens with the line 'Mother died today'?
questions.fun_fact: Camus won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1957 at the age of 44.

questions.question: Which Russian author wrote 'Dead Souls' and the short story 'The Overcoat'?
questions.fun_fact: Dostoevsky is said to have remarked that Russian writers all 'came out of Gogol's Overcoat'.

questions.question: Anish Kapoor's mirror-like Chicago sculpture 'Cloud Gate' is nicknamed what?
questions.fun_fact: Its stainless steel plates were welded and polished so smoothly that no seams are visible.

questions.question: Which Romantic poet wrote 'I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud', about daffodils?
questions.fun_fact: He drew on his sister Dorothy's journal entry about seeing a field of daffodils.

questions.question: Which English architect designed the new St Paul's Cathedral in London after the Great Fire of 1666?
questions.fun_fact: The building was completed in 1710 and its dome is among the largest in the world.

questions.question: In 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland', what does Alice follow down the rabbit hole?
questions.fun_fact: Author Charles Dodgson was a maths lecturer at Oxford and wrote under the name Lewis Carroll.

questions.question: The Pulitzer Prize is administered by which American university?
questions.fun_fact: It is named after the newspaper publisher Joseph Pulitzer, who left money for it in his will.

questions.question: Which Dutch painter is known for 'Girl with a Pearl Earring'?
questions.fun_fact: It is a 'tronie', a study of a face rather than a portrait of a specific person, so the model's identity is unknown.

questions.question: At which King's Cross platform do students board the Hogwarts Express?
questions.fun_fact: Real King's Cross has a trolley half-stuck in a wall with a sign, which is a favourite photo stop.

questions.question: Which narrator opens 'Moby-Dick' with the words 'Call me ...'?
questions.fun_fact: Herman Melville's book flopped at first and was only recognised as a classic decades after his death.

questions.question: Who wrote 'War and Peace'?
questions.fun_fact: His wife Sophia reportedly copied out the huge manuscript by hand several times.

questions.question: Which poet from Amherst, Massachusetts wrote almost 1,800 poems, most of them found after her death?
questions.fun_fact: Dickinson published only a handful of poems in her lifetime, and her sister found the rest in a drawer.

questions.question: In which year was the Mona Lisa stolen from the Louvre?
questions.fun_fact: The thief, an Italian glazier, hid the painting in his Paris flat for two years. The theft is what made the Mona Lisa world-famous.

questions.question: What did Andy Warhol call his New York studio, famous for its silver foil walls?
questions.fun_fact: It became a hangout for artists, musicians and celebrities, and Warhol produced prints there almost on an assembly line.

questions.question: Which American painter made 'American Gothic', showing a farmer with a pitchfork next to a woman?
questions.fun_fact: The models were Wood's dentist and his sister, not a married couple.

questions.question: Hilary Mantel is the only woman to have won the Booker Prize twice, for which pair of novels?

answers.text: Wolf Hall and Bring Up the Bodies
The Remains of the Day and Never Let Me Go
Life of Pi and Oscar and Lucinda

questions.fun_fact: Both books follow the rise of Thomas Cromwell at the court of Henry VIII.

questions.question: Edward Hopper's painting 'Nighthawks' shows people in what kind of place?
questions.fun_fact: The painting dates from 1942 and now hangs in the Art Institute of Chicago.

questions.question: Piet Mondrian's famous grid paintings combine black lines with which set of colours?
questions.fun_fact: His 'Broadway Boogie Woogie' was inspired by the street grid and jazz of New York.

questions.question: Who wrote the vampire novel 'Dracula'?
questions.fun_fact: Stoker was Irish and never visited Transylvania, the novel's setting, instead researching in libraries.

questions.question: Which two German brothers collected fairy tales such as 'Hansel and Gretel'?
questions.fun_fact: They were scholars of language, and their first collection appeared in 1812.

questions.question: What causes the splash in David Hockney's painting 'A Bigger Splash'?

answers.text: An unseen diver jumping off the board

questions.fun_fact: Hockney painted it in 1967, and the diver never appears, so only the aftermath is shown.

questions.question: Who is the student at the centre of Dostoevsky's 'Crime and Punishment'?
questions.fun_fact: The novel is set in St Petersburg and the first half is largely about his crime.

questions.question: Which Spanish painter made 'The Third of May 1808', showing soldiers executing civilians?
questions.fun_fact: The painting shows French troops shooting Madrid citizens, and it inspired Manet and Picasso.

questions.question: Before it became an art museum, the Louvre in Paris was what?
questions.fun_fact: It began as a medieval fortress and opened as a public museum in 1793, during the French Revolution.

questions.question: 'It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.' This opens which novel?
questions.fun_fact: Jane Austen first called it 'First Impressions' and published it anonymously.

questions.question: Which Mexican painter is famous for her many striking self-portraits and her unibrow?
questions.fun_fact: She lived much of her life in the 'Casa Azul', the blue house in Mexico City that is now a museum.

questions.question: The Alhambra, a palace-fortress complex built by Moorish rulers, is in which Spanish city?
questions.fun_fact: Its walls are covered in intricate geometric patterns, because Islamic art avoids depicting people.

questions.question: Edvard Munch, painter of 'The Scream', came from which country?
questions.fun_fact: One version of the painting was stolen from the National Gallery in Oslo in 1994, on the day the Winter Olympics opened.

questions.question: What is the name of the hobbit hero of 'The Hobbit'?
questions.fun_fact: Tolkien reportedly wrote the first line while marking exam papers, on a blank page.

questions.question: Which London museum of modern art is housed in a former power station?
questions.fun_fact: The Bankside Power Station was turned into the museum in 2000, and the old chimney still stands.

questions.question: In 'Peter Pan', who is the pirate captain with a hook for a hand?
questions.fun_fact: J. M. Barrie gave the rights to the play to Great Ormond Street Hospital in London.

questions.question: Jean-Michel Basquiat first became known as a graffiti artist under which tag?
questions.fun_fact: He and a friend tagged cryptic poetic phrases around Lower Manhattan, signed with the tag, before he turned to canvas.

questions.question: Which T. S. Eliot poem begins with the line 'April is the cruellest month'?
questions.fun_fact: Ezra Pound heavily edited the 1922 poem, cutting it to roughly half its original length.

questions.question: What is the name of the miser visited by three ghosts in 'A Christmas Carol'?
questions.fun_fact: Dickens published it in 1843 and the first print run sold out within days.

questions.question: In 'The Three Musketeers', what is the name of the young Gascon who joins them?
questions.fun_fact: Alexandre Dumas wrote the novel in 1844 and gave the group the motto 'All for one, one for all'.

questions.question: Which Russian author wrote 'Doctor Zhivago' and was pressured to decline the 1958 Nobel Prize?
questions.fun_fact: The Soviet authorities denounced the book and forced him to refuse the prize.

questions.question: J. M. W. Turner's 'The Fighting Temeraire' shows an old warship being towed away to be what?
questions.fun_fact: The ship had fought at Trafalgar; the painting topped a 2005 BBC poll for Britain's favourite painting.

questions.question: What does Miss Havisham still wear decades after being jilted in 'Great Expectations'?
questions.fun_fact: She also stopped all the clocks in her house at the moment she received the news.

questions.question: Who narrates F. Scott Fitzgerald's 'The Great Gatsby'?
questions.fun_fact: Gatsby stares at a green light on the end of Daisy's dock, one of literature's best-known symbols.

questions.question: The 'Inferno' is the first part of which epic poem by Dante?
questions.fun_fact: Dante is guided through Hell by the Roman poet Virgil.

questions.question: Which Swiss sculptor is known for extremely thin, elongated figures such as 'Walking Man'?
questions.fun_fact: One cast of 'Walking Man' sold for more than 100 million dollars in 2010.

questions.question: What is the traditional painting technique called in which pigment is applied to wet plaster?
questions.fun_fact: The word 'fresco' comes from the Italian for 'fresh', because the artist must finish before the plaster dries.

questions.question: Which Czech artist became famous for Art Nouveau posters of the actress Sarah Bernhardt?
questions.fun_fact: His flowing, decorative style defined Art Nouveau, and he later painted the 'Slav Epic' cycle.

questions.question: Which Austrian painter made the gold-covered painting 'The Kiss' around 1907?
questions.fun_fact: Klimt used real gold leaf, and the painting hangs in the Belvedere in Vienna.

questions.question: Which Italian painter created 'The Birth of Venus', showing the goddess arriving on a shell?
questions.fun_fact: The painting was commissioned by the Medici family and is painted in tempera on canvas.

questions.question: In which city did Anne Frank and her family hide during World War II?
questions.fun_fact: The Secret Annex was behind her father's office, and her diary has been translated into more than 60 languages.

questions.question: Which Dutch painter created the fantastical triptych 'The Garden of Earthly Delights'?
questions.fun_fact: The three panels run from Paradise through a crowded pleasure garden to a nightmarish Hell.

questions.question: Mark Rothko is best known for large paintings made of soft blocks of colour. Which movement is he associated with?
questions.fun_fact: He wanted viewers to stand close and be enveloped, and preferred his paintings hung low in dim light.

questions.question: Which American artist became known as 'Jack the Dripper' for pouring paint onto canvases laid on the floor?
questions.fun_fact: Working above the canvas let him move all the way around it, so his paintings have no clear top or bottom.

questions.question: Raphael's fresco 'The School of Athens' is in which city?
questions.fun_fact: The central figures are Plato and Aristotle, and Plato is often said to have Leonardo's face.

questions.question: In which year was the first part of Cervantes' 'Don Quixote' published?
questions.fun_fact: The second part only followed in 1615, partly because an unknown author had published a fake sequel in 1614. Cervantes mocks him in it.

questions.question: In which year was George Orwell's 'Nineteen Eighty-Four' published?
questions.fun_fact: Orwell wrote the book while seriously ill on the remote Scottish island of Jura. He died a few months after it came out.

questions.question: Which Romantic poet wrote 'Ozymandias', about a ruined statue in the desert?
questions.fun_fact: He wrote it in 1818 and it ends with the line 'Look on my works, ye Mighty, and despair!'

questions.question: What is a 'triptych' in art?

answers.text: An artwork made of three panels
A painting using only three colours

questions.fun_fact: Medieval altarpieces were often triptychs, with side panels that folded shut like doors.

questions.question: Roy Lichtenstein's pop art paintings imitated the look of what?
questions.fun_fact: He even reproduced the printing dots, known as Ben-Day dots, by hand at giant size.

questions.question: In which English city was the painter David Hockney born?
questions.fun_fact: He later moved to Los Angeles, where he painted his sunny pool pictures such as 'A Bigger Splash'.

questions.question: Which creatures give Macbeth his dangerous prophecy?
questions.fun_fact: Superstitious theatre people avoid saying the name 'Macbeth' inside a theatre and call it 'the Scottish play'.

questions.question: Which Catalan architect designed the still-unfinished Sagrada Família church in Barcelona?
questions.fun_fact: Construction began in 1882 and is still ongoing, which makes it one of the longest building projects in modern Europe.

questions.question: The Mexican artist Frida Kahlo was married to which muralist?
questions.fun_fact: The couple married, divorced and then married each other again within about a year.

questions.question: Leonardo's 'The Last Supper' is painted on what?

answers.text: The wall of a monastery dining hall
A canvas hung in a cathedral

questions.fun_fact: His experimental technique on dry plaster started flaking within decades, so it has been restored many times.

questions.question: In Robert Frost's famous poem, two roads diverge in a what?
questions.fun_fact: Frost meant it partly as a gentle joke on a friend who could never decide which path to take.

questions.question: Which scheming character manipulates Othello into a jealous rage?
questions.fun_fact: Iago has more lines than Othello himself.

questions.question: Which American architect designed Fallingwater, a house built over a waterfall in Pennsylvania?
questions.fun_fact: Wright designed it in the 1930s for the Kaufmann family, who first expected a house with a view of the falls, not above them.

questions.question: Frank Gehry designed the titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum in which Spanish city?
questions.fun_fact: Its 1997 opening helped revive the city and gave rise to the term 'Bilbao effect' for architecture-led regeneration.

questions.question: The Bauhaus, a famous school of design and architecture, was founded in 1919 in which country?
questions.fun_fact: The Nazis forced it to close in 1933, and many teachers emigrated and spread its style worldwide.

questions.question: Who was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1913?
questions.fun_fact: He also wrote the words of the national anthems of both India and Bangladesh.

questions.question: The Turner Prize is awarded each year by which London-based gallery group?
questions.fun_fact: Past winners include Grayson Perry, who collected his 2003 prize dressed as his alter ego Claire.

questions.question: The Little Mermaid statue in Copenhagen honours a story by which author?
questions.fun_fact: The bronze statue was donated in 1913 and has been beheaded and splashed with paint more than once.

questions.question: Through which piece of furniture do the children enter Narnia?
questions.fun_fact: C. S. Lewis published the first Narnia book in 1950, and the saga has seven books.

questions.question: Why does the Leaning Tower of Pisa lean?

answers.text: It was built on soft, shifting ground

questions.fun_fact: It began to tilt in the 12th century while the upper floors were still being built, and engineers stabilised it in the 1990s.

questions.question: Which poet wrote the autobiography 'I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings'?
questions.fun_fact: She read a poem at Bill Clinton's presidential inauguration in 1993.

questions.question: Which Dutch master painted 'The Night Watch', a scene that is actually set in daylight?
questions.fun_fact: Darkened varnish over the centuries gave the painting its nighttime look and its nickname.

questions.question: Which American painter is best known for her large close-ups of flowers?
questions.fun_fact: She later moved to New Mexico, where she painted desert landscapes and sun-bleached animal bones.

questions.question: In Mary Shelley's novel, who or what is 'Frankenstein'?

answers.text: The scientist who creates the creature
The village where the story is set

questions.fun_fact: The creature has no name in the book, and the confusion started with later stage and film adaptations.

questions.question: The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles are named after artists from which period?
questions.fun_fact: Leonardo, Donatello, Michelangelo and Raphael were the creators' picks, and the show jokes that Raphael is the cool but rude one.

questions.question: Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn grew up beside which river?
questions.fun_fact: Mark Twain took his pen name from a riverboat call meaning two fathoms deep.
